  Rafael Gonzalez

  members to notify the City of their need to participate remotely as late

  Government Code section 54953(f). All such meetings will be

 CITY PLANNING COMMISSION AGENDA  MARCH 15, 2023

  NEXT SCHEDULED CITY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

  Tuesday, March 28, 2023 at 7:00 P.M.
  City Hall East – City Council Chambers

  Availability of staff reports: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating
  to each item of business described hereinabove are available on the City’s Home Page at
  www.elmonteca.gov or https://www.ci.el-monte.ca.us/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-2.
  You may also call the Planning Division at (626) 258-8626 for more information.

  Individuals with special needs: The City of El Monte wishes to assist individuals with special
  needs. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to
  participate in this meeting, please contact the Planning Division at (626) 258-8626. Notification
  48 hours prior to the meeting will enable us to make reasonable arrangements to ensure
  accessibility to this meeting. [28 Code of Federal Regulations 35.102-35.104 ADA Title II]

  General explanation of how the meeting is conducted:
  1. The staff report is presented by City Planning staff.
  2. The City Planning Commissioners ask questions if necessary for clarification.
  3. The City Planning Commission Chair opens the public hearing.
  4. The applicant makes a presentation to the City Planning Commission.
  5. Individuals speaking in favor of the project address the Commission.
  6. Individuals speaking against the project address the Commission.
  7. The applicant responds to project opponents.
  8. The public hearing is closed.
  9. City Planning Commission members discuss the project.
  10. City Planning Commission members vote on the project.
  11. At the next scheduled Commission meeting, which is usually two weeks after the hearing, a
  resolution confirming the Commission action will be adopted.
  12. Any interested party who disagrees with the City Planning Commission decision may appeal
  the Commission’s decision to the City Council within 10 calendar days of the adoption of the
  resolution. Any appeal filed must be directed to the City Clerk’s Office and must be
  accompanied by a fee of $868.00 or $3,094.00 (depending on the type of project). Any
  individual that received notice of this meeting from the City of El Monte will receive notice of
  an appeal, if one is filed.

8.1  Design Review (DR) No. 16-22 & Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 08-22

Address/Location: 4097 Temple City Boulevard (APNs: 8592-006-019, 8592-006-020, 8592-
007-051, 8592-007-074, 8592-007-075, & 8592-007-076)

Request: The applicant is requesting to construct a new 100,465 square foot (SF) industrial
warehouse building consisting of 90,350 SF of warehouse space (including 19,995 SF of freezer
storage and 4,245 SF of mezzanine area) and 10,115 SF of office space on property that is 4.6
acres (or 199,935 SF) in size. The proposed project also includes a secured service yard with
13 loading docks, 90 open parking spaces, and approximately 16,907 SF of landscaping. An
employee-only parking lot is proposed to occupy the south-western portion of the property that is
located within the City of Rosemead and a majority of the project site is located within the City of
El Monte’s M-1 (Light Manufacturing) and M-2 (General Manufacturing) zones. This request is
pursuant to Chapters 17.122 and 17.123 of the El Monte Municipal Code (EMMC).

Senior Planner Bu provided a PowerPoint presentation.

Public Comments:

•  John Killen (Xebec Building Company, Inc.) provided background on the proposed
  development/business and confirmed that his team reviewed the recommended conditions of
  approval and have accepted them. Killen confirmed that two (2) truck drivers will be employed
  by the business while other truck drivers visiting the site will be from general truck delivery
  companies. The property will include solar panels and drought tolerant landscaping.

•  Jennifer Wu (Michael Baker International) added that there will be a total of 53 daily truck trips
  generated from the project while the current existing use generates about 58 daily truck trips.

Motion: Following the discussion, it was moved by Commissioner Peralta to approve DR No. 16-
22 and CUP No. 08-22 with the added/modified conditions of approval; seconded by Vice-
Chairperson Nuño.

Motion carried 4 - 0.

8.2 Tentative Tract Map (TTM) No. 073985, Minor Design Review (MDR) No. 04-23 &
  Density Bonus (DB) No. 01-22

Address/Location: 11605 Garvey Avenue & 3015 La Madera Avenue
  (APNs: 8566-018-030 & -021)

Request: The Applicant is requesting approval to consolidate two (2) parcels totaling 31,830±
SF in size into one (1) parcel to develop a vacant site with a mixed-use development composed
of two (2) three (3)-story buildings with a total of 24 affordable housing condominium units and
4,586 SF of ground floor commercial space (located in Building 1, facing Garvey Avenue). One

  FEBRUARY 14, 2023 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES | 2
 (1) level of subterranean parking with 33 off-street parking spaces (14 residential and 19
commercial) is provided. The subject site is located within the M/MU (Mixed/Multi-Use) zone.
This request is made pursuant to the requirements of Chapters 16.08, 17.100, and 17.122 of
the El Monte Municipal Code (EMMC).

Chairperson Wong stated that it is recommended by staff that the item be continued to the next
Planning Commission meeting.

Motion: Following the discussion, it was moved by Commissioner Tamashiro to continue TTM
No. 073985, MDR No. 04-23, & DB No. 01-22 to the next meeting; seconded by Commissioner
Peralta.

Motion carried 4 - 0.

  REPORTS AND OTHER ITEMS

9. Director’s Report:

•  Deputy Director Mikaelian advised the Commissioners that it may be appropriate to elect a
  new chairperson and vice-chairperson for the Planning Commission and a new Zoning
  Review Committee member and alternate due to the new year. Mikaelian also informed the
  Commission that at the next meeting there will be a study session on annual zoning code
  updates. In addition, Mikaelian shared that Senior Planner Bu has recently been inaugurated
  to Pasadena Heritage as a Board Member.

•  Commissioner Peralta suggested that the elections are postponed to the next meeting as the
  full body of the Commission was not present. All of the Commissioners agreed.

10. City Attorney’s Report:

•  City Attorney Tabares provided an update on AB361 and the new provisions for remote
  participation at public meetings that are applicable to AB2449. Therefore, the Commissioners
  will be required to attend public meetings in-person at the first meeting of March. In addition,
  Tabares wished everyone a happy Valentines Day and congratulated Senior Planner Bu on
  his new position.

•  Chairperson Wong inquired if a remote participation option will be available for the public and
  if there will be upcoming legislative bills that address the option. Tabares responded that the
  option would need to be determined by City Council and that there are legislative bills being
  considered.

11. Commissioner Comments:

•  Commissioner Tamashiro inquired if there will be an upcoming ethics training session for the
  Commissioners. Deputy Director Mikaelian responded that there is a two (2) year compliance
  period to take the training session. City Attorney Tabares responded that she will follow up

•  Vice-Chairperson Nuño wished everyone a happy Valentines Day and congratulated Senior

•  Chairperson Wong wished everyone a happy Valentines Day and congratulated Senior

BACKGROUND:

The attached 2022 Housing Element Annual Report (Exhibit B) describes the City’s
progress in meeting the City’s Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) goals
pursuant to Government Code Section 65584 and the City’s efforts to remove
governmental constraints, which may influence the maintenance, improvement, and
development of housing pursuant to State Law. The Housing Element Annual Report
includes the calendar year of 2022. The 2022 reporting year is the second reporting year
of the 6th cycle of the current Housing Element. The last Annual Report submitted to HCD
was for calendar year 2021.

  Planning Commission 3/15/23
  2022 Housing Element Annual Report – Page 1 of 9
 EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
2021-2029 Housing Element (6th Cycle)
(Adopted by El Monte City Council on 2/01/2022)

Per the requirements set forth by the California Department of Housing and Community
Development (HCD), each jurisdiction is required to create an annual report on the status
and progress in implementing the housing element of its general plan using forms and
definitions adopted by HCD. Furthermore, the annual housing report must be submitted
to HCD and the Governor’s Office of Planning and Research that includes data for 2022,
since the last report submitted to HCD was for calendar year 2021. The City adopted its
current General Plan in 2011 (updated in 2022) and the current Housing Element in 2022
(for HCD’s 6th Cycle, which covers the years 2021 through 2029).

Table 1 below shows the number of units that were permitted for the calendar year 2022
by income category. The total RHNA allocation for the 6th Housing Element cycle (2021
through 2029) is 8,502 units. In addition, the total number is allocated to the following
income categories: Very Low – 1,797; Low – 853; Moderate – 1,233; and Above Moderate
– 4,619.

As shown on the following tables, a total of 855 housing units were reported for the year
of 2022. From 2021 through 2022, a total of 949 housing units were permitted . Therefore,
a total of 7,553 housing units remain to be permitted for the entire 6th RHNA cycle. The
2022 reporting year is the second reporting year of the 6th cycle of the current Housing
Element.

  The Planning Commission of the City of El Monte, County of Los Angeles,

State of California, does hereby find, determine and resolve as follows:

  WHEREAS, the City of El Monte’s current Housing Element was adopted

in February 2022; and

  WHEREAS, the Housing Element is one of seven mandatory elements of

a General Plan required by the State of California; and

  WHEREAS, the Housing Element must be updated every eight years and

reviewed for consistency with the State Department of Housing and Community

Development; and

  WHEREAS, California Government Code Section 65400 mandates that

cities submit an Annual Progress Report on the status of the General Plan and its

implementation to their legislative bodies, the Governor’s Office of Planning and

Research (OPR) and the Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD);

and

  WHEREAS, the Annual Progress Report is required to include a) the state

of the Plan and the progress of its implementation; b) the progress in meeting its share

of regional housing needs and local efforts to remove governmental constraints to the

March 15,2023, attached hereto as Exhibit A in accordance with the Guidelines adopted

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission hereby recommends that the City

  ANNUAL ZONING CODE AMENDMENT UPDATES

BACKGROUND

On June 21, 2022, the City Council adopted the Comprehensive Zoning Code Updates.
Staff will then return annually to complete updates, as needed. This Study Session is to
go over key items that are being revised or added as part of the 2023 Annual Zoning
Code Updates. They include the following:

  •  Chapter 17.24 – Multiple-family Residential: Add new qualifying items to receive
  a Floor Area Ratio (FAR) bonus. Add new Subsection on recreational amenities.
  •  Section 17.80.050 – General Procedures: Add Subsection on Special Sign
  Districts.
  •  Chapter 17.102 – Inclusionary Housing: Add new Zoning Code Chapter (Housing
  Element Implementation Program).
  •  Chapter 17.104 – Affordable Housing in Commercial Areas: Add new Zoning
  Code Chapter (State Bill Requirement).
  •  Section 17.110.080 – Religious Institutions Housing: Add new Section (Housing
  Element Implementation Program).
  •  Chapter 17.120 – Zoning Clearance and Administrative Permits: Revise Chapter
  title to “Zoning Clearances & Business Permits.”
  o Revise Zoning Clearance to “Staff Level Zoning Clearance.”
  o Revise Administrative Permit to “Director Level Zoning Clearance.”

  Code Amendment No. 810
  Page 1
   o Add “Business Occupancy Permit.”
  •  Chapter 17.122 – Design and Minor Design Review: Update applicability
  thresholds.
  •  Chapter 17.124 – Temporary Use Permits. Add new Chapter.
  •  Chapter 17.127 – Planned Residential Developments: Update applicability
  requirements and permitted exceptions.

Staff has also completed a Comprehensive update of the City’s Subdivision Ordinance
(Title 16).

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission receive the study session presentation
and provide comments. Staff will then return with a Resolution and Draft Ordinance.
